title: Earn $1,000+ a Month Selling AI Prompts in 2025 - A Practical Guide
excerpt: People keep asking if selling AI prompts is real money or just Twitter hype. Here is a practical way to test it without quitting your day job.
metaDescription: A practical guide to selling AI prompts for side income: where to list, how to price, what to write, and mistakes that kill sales.
author: Ali Hamza
coverImageAlt: Team collaborating around a laptop in a bright office
body:
## Is this still worth trying?

A lot of "make money with AI" posts read like a brochure. I care about a simpler question: can someone with a laptop and a free ChatGPT account test this without burning a month?

Short answer: yes, if you treat prompts like a small digital product, not a lottery ticket.

Buyers are not shopping for magic. They want a prompt that reliably writes ad copy, product descriptions, blog outlines, or image styles so they stop starting from a blank chat every time.

## Where people actually sell prompts

You do not need five marketplaces on day one. Pick one, get a few sales, then expand.

**PromptBase** - Built for text and image prompts. Roughly 20% commission. Good if you want buyers who already understand prompts.

**Etsy** - Works if you already know Etsy SEO. Fees are lower than PromptBase, but you compete with every other digital download.

**Gumroad** - Best when you want your own page, bundles, or a small subscription. Fees sit around 8.5% plus a small per-sale charge.

**Krea and similar image markets** - Useful if you sell Midjourney or Stable Diffusion style packs.

**Upwork** - Not a product storefront. It is custom prompt work for clients. Higher effort, sometimes higher pay.

If I were starting cold today, I would pick **PromptBase or Gumroad**, not all five.

## A simple build loop that does not feel robotic

### 1. Niche down harder than feels comfortable

"ChatGPT prompts" is too wide. "SEO blog outline for SaaS founders" or "Shopify product description for apparel" is easier to rank and easier to sell.

### 2. Write one prompt, then torture-test it

Run it 4-5 times with different inputs. If the output swings wildly, tighten the instructions: tone, length, format, forbidden fluff, and one clear example of a good result.

### 3. Package like a product, not a pastebin

Buyers refund vague listings. Include:

- A title that names the job ("ChatGPT sales email prompt for B2B SaaS")
- What model it targets
- What the buyer gets (prompt + short how-to)
- One sample output screenshot

### 4. Price for learning first

Early sales beat perfect pricing.

- **$5-$10**: single prompt + short guide (hobby buyers)
- **$15-$30**: small bundle of 3-5 prompts
- **$50+**: custom prompt + a couple of revisions for agencies

Start low, collect reviews, raise the price later. Listing a $99 "enterprise" option next to a $19 starter pack also helps the middle tier feel reasonable.

### 5. Ship, then promote without a big ad budget

Show before/after outputs on X or LinkedIn. Drop a free sample in the right Reddit threads without spamming. Put your best product link in your email signature. Cross-promote a discount between Gumroad and PromptBase if you list on both.

## Math that keeps you honest

Hitting $1,000/month at a $15 average sale means roughly 67 paid sales. That is a lot for week one. It is doable over time with bundles, a small subscription, or a few custom gigs mixed in.

If week one is quiet, that is normal. Fix the listing title and sample output before you blame the whole market.

## Mistakes that make the page feel fake

1. Promising guaranteed income. AI outputs vary. Say what the prompt does, not what the buyer will earn.
2. Writing SEO-stuffed titles nobody searches for.
3. Skipping the how-to. Confused buyers refund.
4. Pricing high with zero reviews.
5. Never updating old prompts after models change.

## FAQ

**Do I need a paid AI plan to create sellable prompts?**
Not on day one. Free tiers are enough to draft. A paid plan helps when you need more tests and faster iteration.

**Can I list the same prompt on multiple sites?**
Yes. Slightly change the title or add a small bonus so you are not dumping identical listings everywhere.

**What about legal stuff?**
Do not paste copyrighted text into the prompt pack. Add a simple note that the buyer can use the generated output commercially.

## Bottom line

Selling prompts will not replace a full-time job overnight. It can be a clean side income if you niche down, test the prompt until it is boringly consistent, and sell it like a real product.

Start with one niche and one marketplace. Improve from real buyer feedback. That beats another generic "AI roadmap" every time.
